extra_misconceptions.fact: Smoke inhalation and toxic gases like carbon monoxide and hydrogen cyanide cause far more fire deaths than direct thermal burns.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Visible flames cause the majority of fatalities during residential structure fires rather than invisible combustion gases.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The fire tetrahedron adds a fourth element, the uninhibited chemical chain reaction, to fuel, heat, and an oxidizing agent.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The fire triangle and the fire tetrahedron represent the exact same three components needed to sustain combustion.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thermal radiation travels in straight electromagnetic waves without air currents, whereas convection transfers heat via rising fluids.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Radiant heat requires rising air currents to carry thermal energy from a fireplace across a room to nearby furniture.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An oxygen-starved fire in the decay stage can violently explode in a backdraft if a door or window is opened and introduces fresh air.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A room fire in its decay stage is completely safe to enter because the visible flames have died down to glowing embers.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a flame when a chemical agent interrupts the chain reaction of the fire tetrahedron?
Which physical mechanism transfers thermal energy across an empty room to ignite curtains that never touch the flame?
Which physical indicator signals that an enclosed room fire is transitioning from the growth stage into flashover?
Why is it dangerous to stand upright while escaping a smoke-filled room where carbon monoxide and superheated gases collect?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Spraying the tops of flames wastes extinguishing agent; you must aim at the base of the fire where the fuel is actually burning.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Aiming a fire extinguisher directly at the tallest tips of the flames puts out a fire faster than aiming at the base.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High-temperature cooking oil fires require a Class K wet chemical extinguisher that forms a soapy foam blanket to prevent re-ignition.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A standard multipurpose ABC dry chemical extinguisher is the safest and most effective choice for commercial deep-fat fryer fires.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Removing a fire blanket too early exposes hot oil above its autoignition temperature to fresh oxygen, causing immediate re-ignition.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulling a fire blanket off a smothered grease pan after thirty seconds is safe once the visible smoke stops escaping.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Even a brief discharge allows propellant gas to leak past the valve seal over time, so any used extinguisher must be recharged or replaced.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A fire extinguisher that has only been sprayed for two seconds can be returned to its mounting bracket for future emergencies.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should you aim the extinguisher nozzle during the sweep step of the PASS method so you do not scatter burning fuel?
Why is it dangerous to spray a Class A pressurized water extinguisher onto an energized Class C electrical panel?
What pressure gauge reading and pin inspection confirm that a multipurpose ABC dry chemical extinguisher is ready for use?
Where should you tuck your hands behind a fire blanket when placing it over a burning pan to shield your skin from rising heat?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Greasy ointments trap heat in the tissue and ice causes frostbite damage; cool thermal burns only with cool running water for ten minutes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying butter, ointment, or ice directly to a fresh second-degree burn cools the damaged skin tissue safely and quickly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Intact blisters form a sterile biological barrier over raw dermis, and breaking them exposes the burn wound to severe bacterial infection.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Popping intact fluid blisters on a second-degree burn speeds up skin healing and relieves painful pressure safely.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Loose clothing catches stray flames easily, and synthetic fibers like polyester melt into hot plastic that fuses directly to burned skin.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Loose-fitting polyester athletic shirts offer better protection around a campfire than snug heavyweight cotton or wool garments.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scalds from spilled hot beverages, soup, and overly hot tap water are the leading cause of burn injuries among young children.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Direct contact with open flames causes more pediatric emergency room burn injuries each year than hot liquids and steam.

extra_socratic_questions: Why should you cover your face with your hands during the stop, drop, and roll maneuver when your clothing catches fire?
What happens to loose synthetic fabrics like nylon or polyester when exposed to high heat compared to heavy cotton or wool?
What maximum temperature setting on a home water heater thermostat prevents accidental tap-water scald burns for children?
Under what condition must you leave burned clothing in place while cooling a thermal injury with cool running water?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unintended human mistakes are classified as accidental fires, whereas incendiary fires are deliberately ignited under unlawful circumstances.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every fire that starts from human carelessness, such as an unattended candle or stove, is classified as an incendiary fire.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Undetermined is a valid scientific classification used whenever physical damage or insufficient evidence prevents proving a single cause.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Classifying a fire cause as undetermined means investigators failed to do their job and can never reopen the case later.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Premature overhaul destroys burn patterns and washes away trace accelerants, compromising the physical evidence needed for investigation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Firefighters should wash down and shovel out charred debris immediately after extinguishing a suspicious fire to make the building safe.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Canine alerts only guide where to collect debris samples; gas chromatography laboratory testing is required to confirm ignitable liquids.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A hydrocarbon-sniffing Accelerant Detection Canine alert at a fire scene is sufficient proof by itself to convict someone of arson.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical char patterns on walls and framing help a fire investigator trace a blaze back to its point of origin?
Under what condition must an investigator classify a structure fire as undetermined rather than accidental or incendiary?
Why must fire investigators seal debris samples in airtight metal cans when testing for ignitable liquid accelerants at a scene?
What legal elements beyond an incendiary cause classification must a prosecutor prove in court to convict a suspect of arson?

extra_misconceptions.fact: High-wattage heating appliances overheat extension cords and power strips, so they must be plugged directly into dedicated wall outlets.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plug-in power strips with built-in circuit breakers allow you to safely run a portable space heater and microwave on an extension cord.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Water sinks below hot oil and flashes into steam, spraying flaming grease everywhere; slide a metal lid over the pan and turn off the burner.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pouring a cup of tap water onto a burning skillet of cooking oil cools the pan and puts out the kitchen grease fire quickly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cut evergreen trees absorb water daily and dry out rapidly indoors; a dry tree can engulf an entire living room in under thirty seconds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A fresh cut Christmas tree only needs water in its stand during the first week indoors before the trunk seals itself off.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Failing lithium-ion batteries vent toxic gas and jet flames rapidly, so charging them in a doorway can block your only escape route.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Charging an electric bike or scooter battery overnight right inside your bedroom doorway keeps the battery safe from outdoor cold.

extra_socratic_questions: What immediate actions should you take if oil in a skillet ignites on the stove instead of carrying the pan to the sink?
Which physical signs warn that a rechargeable lithium-ion battery pack is failing and at risk of thermal runaway?
What minimum clearance distance must you keep between a portable space heater and any curtains, bedding, or furniture?
Why is cleaning the removable lint screen before every load not enough to prevent a clothes dryer exhaust duct fire over time?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Flammable vapors evaporating from the liquid actually ignite, and heavy gasoline fumes can travel invisibly across a floor to distant sparks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Liquid gasoline itself burns directly, so a sealed fuel container is only dangerous if an open flame touches the liquid surface.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Milk jugs degrade and glass shatters on impact; store gasoline only in red UL-approved safety containers in a ventilated shed or garage.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any sturdy plastic milk jug or glass jar with a tight screw cap is safe for storing leftover lawn mower gasoline in a garage.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Drying oils generate exothermic heat as they oxidize, causing piled rags to ignite spontaneously unless laid flat outside or sealed in water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rags soaked with linseed oil or wood stain can be tossed into a closed plastic trash can in the garage until garbage collection day.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A hot exhaust muffler exceeds the autoignition temperature of gasoline vapors, so you must let the engine cool completely before refueling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Refueling a lawn mower while the engine is still hot is safe as long as you turn the ignition switch off and use a funnel.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must you place a portable gasoline container flat on the ground rather than in a truck bed when filling it at a fuel pump?
Why does the high vapor density of gasoline make storing fuel cans near a basement water heater pilot light so dangerous?
Why should you leave a small air space at the top of a UL-approved safety fuel can instead of filling it completely to the brim?
What happens if spilled gasoline contacts a hot lawn mower muffler when a Scout refuels the engine immediately after mowing?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard wet-pipe sprinkler heads are activated individually by a heat-sensitive glass bulb or fusible link directly over the actual fire.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulling a manual fire alarm station or triggering one sprinkler head with heat causes every sprinkler in the building to spray water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wedging a fire-rated stairwell door open defeats building compartmentation and lets toxic smoke fill the vertical evacuation route.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Propping open a heavy stairwell fire door with a wooden wedge is harmless during busy daytime hours to improve hallway airflow.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Elevator shafts act like chimneys for smoke, power failure can trap riders, and heat sensors may recall the cab directly to the burning floor.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Taking the elevator is the fastest and safest way to reach the ground floor during a high-rise hotel fire alarm evacuation.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thick black smoke rapidly obscures overhead exit signs, so counting doors lets you locate the stairwell by touch while crawling low.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Counting the doorways between your hotel room and the nearest stairwell is unnecessary because lighted exit signs stay visible in smoke.

extra_socratic_questions: What specific features should you locate and count on your floor map immediately after checking into a multi-story hotel?
What distinguishes passive fire barriers like fire-rated stairwell doors from active systems like automatic sprinklers?
Why must egress doors in high-occupancy assembly buildings swing outward in the direction of travel and use panic bar hardware?
Why is it dangerous to use an elevator instead of an enclosed fire stairwell when evacuating a multi-story public building?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dirt insulates hot coals so they smolder underground and ignite roots; always drown a fire with water and stir the ashes until cold out.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Burying glowing campfire coals under a thick layer of dirt and sand extinguishes a fire safely when water is scarce at camp.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Water trapped inside porous creek rocks turns to high-pressure steam when heated, causing the stones to explode and throw sharp shrapnel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: River rocks and wet creek stones make the best border for a new campfire ring because moisture inside the stone keeps them cool.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Strike-anywhere match tips contain all chemicals needed for friction ignition, so rubbing together in a pocket can set them on fire.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Safety matches and strike-anywhere matches can be carried loose together in a pants pocket without any risk of accidental ignition.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Leave No Trace requires gathering only dead and downed wood no thicker than an adult wrist so standing snag habitats remain undisturbed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Breaking thick dead branches directly off standing trees is recommended by Leave No Trace to keep campfire fuel dry in damp weather.

extra_socratic_questions: Why should you strike a match away from your body and hold the burned matchstick by its charred head before disposing of it?
What chemical separation keeps a safety match from igniting on a rock, unlike a strike-anywhere match tip?
What physical test confirms that a doused and stirred campfire bed is truly cold out before your patrol leaves the campsite?
Why must you clear duff and pine needles down to bare mineral soil before building a campfire where no established ring exists?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Soil insulates hot coals so they can smolder underground for days, ignite tree roots, and surface later when winds blow away the dirt.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Burying hot campfire coals under dirt or sand extinguishes the fire safely without needing water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Human activities such as unattended campfires, equipment sparks, and debris burning cause roughly 85 percent of U.S. wildland fires.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Lightning strikes cause the vast majority of wildland fires across populated regions of the United States.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many fire-adapted ecosystems rely on periodic low-intensity fires to clear dead brush, recycle soil nutrients, and open serotinous cones.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every wildland fire destroys forest ecosystems permanently and prevents native plants from regenerating.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Indirect costs from watershed erosion, smoke healthcare impacts, lost tourism, and suppression operations often exceed direct property damage.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wildland fire economic losses are limited to the direct cost of replacing burned homes and timber.

extra_socratic_questions: What tactile check confirms a campfire bed has zero lingering embers before a patrol abandons a backcountry site?
What happens to watershed soil structure after a high-severity crown fire compared to a low-intensity surface burn?
Under what condition does relative humidity combined with gusty winds trigger a Red Flag Warning for wildland fuels?
Why is it dangerous to park a vehicle with a hot catalytic converter over dry tall grass at a trailhead?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engines carry pumps, hoses, and water tanks, whereas dedicated ladder trucks specialize in aerial rescue, ventilation, and forcible entry tools.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every fire truck carries a large onboard water tank and high-capacity main pump as its primary firefighting system.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most municipal fire departments respond primarily to emergency medical calls, alongside conducting code inspections and public safety education.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Structural firefighters spend almost all of their shift responding to building fires rather than medical or prevention calls.

extra_misconceptions.fact: SCBA cylinders hold compressed breathing-grade room air because pure oxygen would dangerously accelerate combustion in a fire environment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Self-contained breathing apparatus tanks pump pure oxygen to firefighters working inside smoke-filled structures.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fire prevention staff proactively review building plans, inspect sprinkler systems, enforce occupancy limits, and run community safety programs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Fire prevention divisions only investigate arson scenes after a building has already burned down.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator or onboard equipment distinguishes a Type 1 structural pumper engine from an aerial ladder truck?
Where should a Scout group position themselves inside an active apparatus bay if a dispatch alarm sounds during a tour?
What specific community risk details should you record when interviewing a fire marshal about local code inspections?
Why is it dangerous to store turnout gear inside living quarters instead of a ventilated apparatus bay locker?
